translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the command of God our Savior and of Jesus Christ, our hope,
to Timothy, my true child in the faith: grace, mercy and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
As I urged you to stay in Ephesus when I was going to Macedonia, so that you might instruct certain people not to teach anything different,
and not to devote themselves to Jewish fables and those endless genealogies, which bring about inquiries rather than God's work, which is by faith.
But the goal of the commandment is love from a pure heart and a good conscience and a sincere faith,
which some have failed to reach, and they have turned aside to empty talk.
They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand either what they are saying or the things they make claims about.
But know this: the law is good if anyone keeps it properly.

Know this: the law is not meant for the righteous, but for the lawless and disobedient, the ungodly and sinners, the unworthy and defiled, those who insult their fathers and those who insult their mothers, murderers,
fornicators, men who lie with men, slave-traders, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to the teaching of this life,
according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which has been entrusted to me.
And I am grateful to the one who gave me strength, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he considered me faithful and appointed me to this ministry,
even though I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor and an insulter. But I was shown mercy, because I acted out of ignorance, in unbelief.
And the grace of our Lord overflowed all the more, together with faith and love through Christ Jesus.
The saying is trustworthy and deserves full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and I am the foremost of them.
But I was shown mercy for this reason: so that in me first Jesus Christ might display all his patience, as an example for those who would later believe in him for eternal life.
Now to the King of the ages, the incorruptible, the invisible, the only God, be honor and glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I entrust this command to you, Timothy my child, in keeping with the teachings, the prophecies made earlier about you, so that by them you may fight the good fight,
holding on to faith and a good conscience. Some have thrown this away and have sinned against the faith.
Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan so that they may learn not to blaspheme.
So first of all I urge that supplications, prayers, acts of worship and thanksgivings be made for all people,
and for kings and all rulers, so that we may live in peace and quiet with all godliness and holiness.
for this is good and pleasing before God our Savior,
He wants all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and humans, the man Jesus Christ,
who gave himself as a ransom for all, as a testimony at his own proper time.
For this I was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I am telling the truth, I am not lying), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
I want the men to pray in every place, lifting up holy hands without anger or argument.
Likewise, women should adorn themselves in orderly apparel, with modesty and dignity, not with braided hair, gold, pearls or costly clothing,
but with what is fitting for women who profess the service of God: with good works.
Let a woman learn in silence with all submission.
I do not permit women to teach, nor to have authority over men, but they are to be in quietness.
For Adam was created first, then Eve.
And Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and transgressed the law.
Yet she will be saved through bearing children, if they remain in faith and love and holiness, with dignity.
The saying is trustworthy: if anyone desires the office of bishop, his heart is set on a good work.
A bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, watchful, pure, orderly, hospitable, learned,
not a drunkard, not a brawler, but kind, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money,
one who manages his own household well and keeps his children in submission with all dignity.
If someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he take care of the churches of God?
He must not be a new convert, so that he does not become puffed up and fall into the condemnation of the devil.
Moreover, he must also have a good testimony from those outside, so that he does not fall into reproach and into the snare of the devil.
Deacons likewise must be pure, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not seekers of shameful gain,
holding the mystery of the faith with a pure mind.
And let these also be tested first, and only then let them serve as deacons, if they are blameless.
Their wives likewise must be dignified, not slanderers, but watchful, faithful in all things.
Deacons must be the husbands of one wife, and must manage their children and their own households well.
Those who serve well as deacons gain a good standing for themselves and great boldness in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
I write this to you, and I hope to come to you soon;
but if I am delayed, I write so that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

Undeniably, great is the mystery of the service of God: he who was revealed in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen by angels, preached among the nations, believed in by the world, and taken up in glory.
But the Holy Spirit says plainly that in the last times some will depart from the faith and will follow deceiving spirits and the teachings of demons,
through hypocrisy and lying words, led astray in their own minds,
They forbid marriage and keep people from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving as nourishment by those who believe and know the truth.
For everything God created is good, and nothing is to be rejected that is received with thanksgiving,
for it is made holy by the word of God and by prayer.
Teach this to the brothers, and you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of the faith and of the good teaching that you have followed.
But avoid those profane old wives' tales.
For bodily training is of benefit for a short time, but godliness is of benefit in every way, since it holds the promise of the present life and of the life to come.
This saying is trustworthy and worthy of full acceptance.
For this is why we toil and suffer reproach: we hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all people, and especially of those who believe.
Command these things and teach them.
Let no one look down on your youth, but be an example to the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
Until I come, give your attention to reading, to encouragement, and to teaching.
Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy when the elders laid their hands on you.
Practise these things and devote yourself to them, so that your progress may be evident to everyone.
Watch yourself and your teaching, and persevere in them. By doing this you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.
Do not rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as a father; treat younger men as brothers,
older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, in all purity.
Honour widows who are truly widows.
If a widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to show godliness toward their own household and to honour their parents, for this is pleasing before God.
But the true widow, who has been left all alone, has set her hope on the Lord and continues in supplication and prayer night and day.
But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she lives.
Command these things too, so that they may be blameless.
If anyone does not provide for his own relatives, and especially for his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let no one be enrolled as a widow who is under sixty years of age. She must have been the wife of one husband

and be well known for good works: that she has raised children, that she has shown hospitality to strangers, that she has washed the feet of the saints, that she has helped those in distress, that she has devoted herself to every good work.
But refuse younger widows, for when their desires lead them to turn away from Christ, they want to marry.
They are under judgment, because they have set aside their first faith.
Along with this they learn idleness, going about from house to house. And they are not only idle, but also chatterers and busybodies, and they say what is improper.
So I want the young women to marry, bear children and manage the household, and to give the adversary no occasion at all for reviling.
For some have already turned aside to follow the devil.
If any believer has widows, let him provide for them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may provide for the other widows.
Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor zealously in the word and in teaching.
For the scripture says: "You shall not muzzle the ox that treads the threshing floor," and: "The laborer is worthy of his wage."
Do not accept an accusation against an elder except on the evidence of two or three witnesses.
Rebuke those who sin in front of everyone, so that the others may be afraid.
I charge you before God and Jesus Christ and the elect angels to keep these things without partiality,
Do not lay hands on anyone hastily, and do not share in another's sins. Keep yourself pure.
Do not drink only water, but take a little wine as well, for your stomach and your frequent illnesses.
The sins of some people are evident beforehand and go ahead of them to judgment; the sins of others follow after them.
Likewise good works are evident beforehand, and those that are otherwise cannot be hidden.
Let all who are under the yoke of slavery count their own masters worthy of all honor, so that the name of God and this teaching may not be blasphemed.

Let those who have believing masters not despise them because they are brothers. Instead, let them serve them all the more, because they are believers and beloved, partners in the good work. Teach and urge these things.
If anyone teaches something else and does not hold to these life-giving words of our Lord Jesus Christ and to the teaching of this godliness,
he is puffed up and knows nothing. Instead he is diseased with disputing and quarrels about words, from which come envy, strife, slanders, evil suspicions,
anger, and the mindset of corrupted people who are lacking in the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain.
But godliness with contentment is in truth great gain.
For we brought nothing into the world; [?] for neither can we carry anything out.
But if we have food and clothing, let that be enough for us.
But those who want to be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many senseless and harmful desires, which plunge people into ruin and destruction.
For the love of money is the root of all evil. Some have longed for it and strayed from the faith, and pierced themselves with many kinds of pain.
But you, man of God, flee from these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience and peace;
Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life to which you were called, and you confessed the good confession before many witnesses.
I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and before Jesus Christ, who testified the good confession before Pontius Pilate,
to keep the commandment spotless and blameless until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which he will show in his own time, he who is the blessed and only Mighty One, the King of kings and Lord of lords,
who alone has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light, whom no one among men has seen or is able to see; to whom be honor and eternal power. Amen.
Command those who are rich in this world not to be haughty, and not to hope in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who gives us all things richly to enjoy;
and to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous givers, ready to share,
and to store up for themselves a good foundation for the time to come, so that they may lay hold of the true life.
O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you, and turn away from the profane, empty novelties of speech and the contradictions of what is falsely called knowledge,
which some have professed and have gone astray from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.
